h1: Olive Oil vs Avocado Oil: Which One Does Your Kitchen Need?
excerpt: Two premium bottles, two different jobs. A cook's comparison of olive oil and avocado oil on flavour, heat, texture and cost per litre in Malaysia.
keyTakeaway: Compare these two as cooking fats, not as health products. Refined avocado oil is near-neutral and its smoke point is the higher of the two, above the 190 to 210 °C published for extra virgin olive oil. Buy avocado where the oil should vanish, olive where the oil is the flavour.

intro: Avocado oil reached Malaysian shelves with a high-heat reputation and a price to match, and shoppers now stand between two expensive bottles trying to work out which one is doing the work.
Held against each other as cooking fats — flavour, heat, texture, cost per litre — they are less rivals than two different tools. One is bought to be tasted. The other is bought to disappear.

sections.heading: What actually separates the two oils

blocks.text: Both are pressed from fruit rather than seed, and both stay liquid at Malaysian room temperature. What matters is what each is for. Extra virgin olive oil carries a flavour you are meant to notice; most avocado oil sold here is refined and near-neutral, chosen because it adds nothing.

items: **Olive oil:** pressed from whole olives, sold here as extra virgin, tasted in the dish.
**Avocado oil:** pressed from avocado flesh, usually refined, close to flavourless.
**Both:** pourable all year here, unlike coconut oil in a cool kitchen.

sections.heading: Flavour: peppery and grassy against buttery and neutral

blocks.text: Extra virgin olive oil tastes of something specific: cut grass, green tomato leaf, bitterness at the back of the tongue and a peppery catch in the throat. Refined avocado oil tastes of very little, a faint buttery weight at most. Neither is a fault; each is the point of that oil.
So the test is short. If the finished plate should taste of the oil, olive earns its price. If the oil should vanish, neutral wins.

sections.heading: Heat, honestly: avocado oil's smoke point is the higher one

blocks.text: Refined avocado oil smokes at a higher temperature than extra virgin olive oil, and no seller should pretend otherwise. Published figures put extra virgin olive oil at 190 to 210 °C, and refined avocado oil sits above that band. For a pan taken to a hard sear, the gap is real.

It matters less than the numbers suggest, because most cooking never nears either ceiling. Tumis and shallow frying run below both. What moves the figure is set out in [olive oil smoke point](/blog/olive-oil-smoke-point-what-heat-it-can-take).

Stop asking which oil is better and ask what the dish needs. Where the oil is tasted, olive answers. Where it has to be invisible, or held very hot, avocado answers. Most kitchens keep both and use each on a different night.

sections.heading: Price per litre, and what is on the shelf in Malaysia

blocks.text: Both cost several times what palm cooking oil does, and the ranking between them moves with brand, grade and bottle size. Compare per litre rather than per bottle, since the bottles rarely match. Avocado oil is a narrow import here; olive oil is stocked far more widely.

Arabian Village comes in 250 ml and 500 ml, with the current price for each on the [products page](/products) and the larger bottle cheaper per litre. In Malaysia it is sold only through Berkat Madinah Store and that seller's own Shopee and TikTok Shop counters — see [where to buy](/shop).

Keeping both is a sensible outcome rather than a failure to decide. A small bottle of extra virgin olive oil for everything served cold or finished with the oil showing, plus a neutral oil for the pan that runs hardest, covers almost every dish.
If your real question is which is better for you, that is one for a doctor or a registered dietitian, not for anyone selling oil. This page compares behaviour in a pan and nothing more.

Reach for avocado oil when the oil should be invisible or the pan is at its hottest. Reach for extra virgin olive oil when the oil is part of the flavour. Its smoke point is the lower of the two, and most home cooking reaches neither.

faqs.q: Is avocado oil or olive oil better for high heat?
faqs.a: Avocado oil, on smoke point alone. Refined avocado oil holds a higher temperature than extra virgin olive oil, which published figures put at 190 to 210 °C. Most home cooking stays well below both.

faqs.q: Can I use olive oil instead of avocado oil?
faqs.a: In anything cooked short of a hard sear, yes. Expect the dish to taste of olive oil, which is the whole point in a dressing or a pasta and a distraction in mayonnaise.

faqs.q: Does avocado oil taste like avocado?
faqs.a: Refined avocado oil barely tastes of anything, a faint buttery weight at most. Unrefined versions keep more of the fruit, but the bottles sold widely in Malaysia are the refined, near-neutral kind.

faqs.q: Which one is more expensive in Malaysia?
faqs.a: It depends on brand, grade and size, so compare per litre rather than per bottle. Avocado oil is the narrower import and turns up in fewer shops; olive oil is stocked far more widely.

faqs.q: Is avocado oil healthier than olive oil?
faqs.a: That is a question for a doctor or a registered dietitian, not for a seller. This page compares the two as cooking fats only: flavour, heat behaviour, texture and cost per litre.

faqs.q: Which oil should I use for salad dressing?
faqs.a: Extra virgin olive oil, unless you want the dressing to taste only of the vinegar and the mustard. Avocado oil is the choice when the other ingredients are meant to carry it alone.
